subject.title: feat(channels): bundle Reef guarded claw-to-claw channel

question: After the concrete packaging, persistence, pairing, reconnect, documentation, and proof blockers are fixed, should bundled Reef accept the documented undated-model pinning risk as part of OpenClaw's supported security boundary?
rationale: The implementation acknowledges that a provider can change an undated model backend without Reef detecting it, so automation cannot determine whether this residual risk is acceptable for a bundled security-focused channel.

options.title: Approve After Blockers
options.body: Fix the concrete blockers, add inspectable live proof, then explicitly accept and document the undated-model risk for bundled Reef.

options.title: Require Dated Pins
options.body: Keep Reef bundled but reject undated model IDs until the provider exposes a verifiable immutable identifier.

options.title: Externalize Reef
options.body: Keep Reef in its owner repository as an external plugin until its trust and persistence boundaries meet bundled-core requirements.

recommendation.title: Approve After Blockers
recommendation.body: Fix the concrete blockers, add inspectable live proof, then explicitly accept and document the undated-model risk for bundled Reef.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch and discussion attribute both the bundling direction and the model-risk decision to this feature owner, who is also identified by repository automation as connected to security operations.
